role: Zsh line editor + fzf fuzzy pickers + modern CLI replacements; the keyboard layer inside every terminal pane

hotkeys.description: bindkey -s macro that types and runs ~/bin/zellij-sessionizer, an fzf picker over ~/work, ~/personal, ~/.config/nvim and ~/.local/share/chezmoi; switches or creates a Zellij session for the chosen dir
hotkeys.notes: Verified live. Shadows the emacs default ⌃F (forward-char), which zsh-autosuggestions treats as a FULL accept (forward-char is in ZSH_AUTOSUGGEST_ACCEPT_WIDGETS, not the partial list). Use → for full accept, ⌥F for partial.

hotkeys.description: Searches history for entries containing what is already typed, instead of plain previous-line
hotkeys.notes: Widget comes from zsh-users/zsh-history-substring-search. The bindkey at line 117 runs BEFORE the turbo-loaded (`zinit wait lucid`) plugin defines the widget; zsh resolves widget names lazily at keypress time, by which point the plugin has loaded. Verified live in an interactive pty: ^[[A → history-substring-search-up. Overrides OMZ's up-line-or-beginning-search.

hotkeys.description: fzf-history-widget; replaces zsh's incremental reverse search
hotkeys.notes: Enabled by `source <(fzf --zsh)` (fzf 0.74.1). Verified active. Also overrides OMZL::key-bindings.zsh, which had bound ^r to history-incremental-search-backward.

hotkeys.description: fzf-file-widget; pastes the selected path onto the command line
fzf-cd-widget; bound to the escape sequence ^[c
hotkeys.notes: Reachable: Ghostty sets `macos-option-as-alt = true` (dot_config/ghostty/config:5) so ⌥C sends ESC c, and Zellij's locked mode only binds Alt+n and Alt+arrows, so ESC c passes through. Verified bound live (^[c → fzf-cd-widget). The widget sets `no_aliases` and runs `builtin cd`, so the `cd`→zoxide `z` alias is bypassed — ⌥C jumps do NOT get recorded in the zoxide database.

hotkeys.description: fzf-completion replaces the default completion widget; `**` before Tab forces the fzf picker for paths, hostnames, PIDs, env vars
hotkeys.notes: Verified live (^I → fzf-completion). fzf falls back to whatever was bound to ^I at load time, so zstyle menu-select completion still works for non-** completions.

hotkeys.description: edit-command-line widget; opens the current buffer in $EDITOR (nvim) and runs it on save+quit
hotkeys.notes: Verified live. Not a zsh built-in — zsh does not bind ^X^E or autoload edit-command-line by default; the OMZ library snippet does both. Useful for long pipelines.

hotkeys.description: forward-char; listed in ZSH_AUTOSUGGEST_ACCEPT_WIDGETS, so at end-of-line it accepts the whole greyed-out suggestion
hotkeys.notes: The primary accept key now that ⌃F is the sessionizer macro. Verified: ^[[C and ^[OC → forward-char, and 9 autosuggest widgets are loaded in an interactive shell.

hotkeys.description: end-of-line; zsh-autosuggestions wraps this widget so it accepts the greyed-out suggestion
hotkeys.notes: Verified live (^E → end-of-line, with autosuggest wrappers installed). Equivalent to → for accepting; both are full accepts.

hotkeys.description: forward-word; the only partial-accept widget actually bound here (ZSH_AUTOSUGGEST_PARTIAL_ACCEPT_WIDGETS contains forward-word plus vi/emacs variants)
hotkeys.notes: Verified bound live (^[F → forward-word). Needs Ghostty's macos-option-as-alt. This is the correct replacement for the commonly-cited ⌃F partial accept — ⌃F was never a partial accept.

Verified live (^U → kill-whole-line). This is zsh's own emacs-mode default, NOT something OMZ sets — OMZL::key-bindings.zsh never binds ^U. backward-kill-line is the bash default, which is why the behaviour surprises people coming from bash.
Verified live (^W → backward-kill-word), a plain zsh emacs default; OMZ leaves it alone (its `bindkey '^W' kill-region` line is commented out).

hotkeys.description: OMZ ships `bindkey -s '\el' '^Q ls\n'` — pushes the current buffer aside and runs `ls` (here the eza alias), then restores the buffer
hotkeys.notes: Live but probably unintended: verified in the bindkey dump as a macro. Shadows the zsh default ⌥L (down-case-word). Only reachable because of macos-option-as-alt.
